Question 4.1

```{r}
#Loading the required R packages
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)

```

```{r}
# Website URL
url <- "https://books.toscrape.com/"

# Read webpage
page <- read_html(url)

```


```{r}
#extracting each book block
books <- page %>%
  html_elements("article.product_pod")


```

```{r}
#extracting titles
title <- books %>%
  html_element("h3 a") %>%
  html_attr("title")

```


```{r}
#extracting prices
price_raw <- books %>%
  html_element(".price_color") %>%
  html_text2()

```

```{r}
#extracting stock availability
availability <- books %>%
  html_element(".availability") %>%
  html_text2()


```

```{r}
#extracting ratings
rating_raw <- books %>%
  html_element(".star-rating") %>%
  html_attr("class")
```

```{r}
#applying regex to extract usable values
price <- str_extract(
  price_raw,
  "[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+"
)

price <- as.numeric(price)


```


```{r}
#extracting the textual rating
rating <- str_extract(
  rating_raw,
  "One|Two|Three|Four|Five"
)

```


```{r}

rating_number <- case_when(
  rating == "One"   ~ 1,
  rating == "Two"   ~ 2,
  rating == "Three" ~ 3,
  rating == "Four"  ~ 4,
  rating == "Five"  ~ 5,
  TRUE ~ NA_real_
)

```


```{r}
#cleaning the stock text
availability <- str_squish(
  availability
)


```

```{r}
#creating the data frame 
books_df <- data.frame(
  title = title,
  price = price,
  rating = rating,
  rating_number = rating_number,
  availability = availability,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

View(books_df)

```

Explanation:
The selected use case was book catalogue analysis using the Books to Scrape website. This website was selected because it is a public web-scraping sandbox and provides structured product information including title, price, rating and stock status. The rvest package was used to extract the HTML content, while regular expressions were applied using stringr to isolate numeric price values and rating categories. The scraped data was converted into an R data frame containing both textual attributes and numerical attributes suitable for later ETL processing.


Question 4.2:

```{r}
#inspecting the data
summary(books_df)

```


```{r}
#checking for missing values
colSums(is.na(books_df))

```

```{r}
#checking for blank strings
colSums(
  books_df == ""
)

```

```{r}
#cleaning the title
books_df$title <- str_squish(
  books_df$title
)

```



```{r}
#standardise availability
books_df$availability <- str_to_lower(
  books_df$availability
)

books_df$availability <- case_when(
  str_detect(books_df$availability, "in stock") ~ "In Stock",
  TRUE ~ "Unknown"
)


```



```{r}
#Imputing missing numerical values

median_price <- median(
  books_df$price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

books_df$price[
  is.na(books_df$price)
] <- median_price


```



```{r}
#applying median rating for missing ratings
median_rating <- median(
  books_df$rating_number,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

books_df$rating_number[
  is.na(books_df$rating_number)
] <- median_rating



```


```{r}
#imputing missing categorical values
books_df$rating[
  is.na(books_df$rating)
] <- "Unknown"

```

```{r}
books_df$availability[
  is.na(books_df$availability) |
  books_df$availability == ""
] <- "Unknown"


```

```{r}
#removing duplicates
books_clean <- books_df %>%
  distinct()

```

```{r}
summary(books_clean)

colSums(is.na(books_clean))

```

```{r}
#exporting to csv
write.csv(
  books_clean,
  "/Users/dani-myburgh/Downloads/books_clean.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

Explanation:
The scraped dataset was cleaned by removing excessive white space, standardising categorical values and checking for missing values and duplicates. Numerical missing values were imputed using the median because the median is less sensitive to extreme values than the mean. Missing categorical values were replaced with Unknown. Duplicate rows were removed before exporting the final cleaned dataset to books_clean.csv.
